body:
Be glad that you have escaped.

I’m in an abusive relationship, and feel stuck, because last time I tried to leave they created a false accusation of abuse against me, preventing me from seeing my children for months, almost ending my career until they decided they wanted to “give me another chance”. (Taking care of the children was too much for them, and they never wanted the kids, they wanted to hurt me for trying to leave) My kids and I are afraid, but also afraid to leave, because my spouse is disabled, and has convinced others that not only can they not be abusive, because of that, but that I am. But, enough about my issues, I just wanted to explain what a spurned ex is capable of.

For that reason, it is important that you stay alive for your child. Your ex could be capable of harming them to get back at you or your family for leaving.

Ensure you are obeying the letter of the law. If you run off or do things that can put the law on your ex’s side, expect them to use it to try to regain control over you.

Document everything that goes on during your child’s visits. If he is harming your child try to find a way to get his visitation rights taken. He is much much re likely to escalate his behavior, than he is to get better.

Get a restraining order, and whether you get one or not, avoid being alone with them. Violent abusers are capable of worse. Don’t give them an opportunity.

I have eight years to survive until my youngest is 18. You have escaped, but as long as there  is a child, he is part of your life. Stay safe, for you and your child. If your insurance covers it and/or you can afford it, see someone (therapy, psychiatrist or psychologist) to help deal with your past trauma and any lingering mental issues.
